rationale:
There's no Lane C trigger today. No named next-gen drug has a new result or regulatory step that became public in the last 48 hours. CagriSema's FDA decision is still pending (keep the decoder pre-built), and CX11 is financial news only. We've also had two decoders in two days (petrelintide 10-25 and elecoglipron 10-26), so Lane P is at its weekly cap.

That leaves the long-form in Lane A. The other playbook examples all clash with recent pieces:
- Hair loss had its own GLP-1 hair-loss long-form on 09-28, inside the 30-day window.
- Protein repeats the 10-21 protein Short (inside the 14-day ban) and the 10-21 What to Eat long-form.
- A bones/muscle long-form would repeat the 10-25 bones Short and the 10-23 grip Short.

So L1 is "What Happens When You Stop Tirzepatide?" It's a named playbook example and evergreen. The body rests on the randomized SURMOUNT-4 withdrawal trial, with new real-world persistence papers as the hook. The radar marked it caution, so the angle is evidence-first and repeats the "don't stop or change on your own" line throughout. It's a different angle from the 09-29 piece (veterans with type 2 diabetes, class-wide, observational).

Shorts:
- **08:00 body-worry slot:** a fresh FLOW kidney-safety paper. It covers semaglutide only, which the body-worry exception allows.
- **13:00 lead:** a tirzepatide-first head-to-head on SURPASS-2. We've never used that trial in a Short, so it passes the variety guard.
- **20:00:** a spin-off of L1 to meet the spin-off rule. Its CTA names L1 only after an oEmbed check confirms the link. Otherwise it falls back to "follow for more" and doesn't count toward Exp D, which avoids repeating the 10-26 hold.

The carousel reuses only the verified text from the 10-25 bones Short, our second-best Short.

Body systems are spread out: weight and appetite, kidneys, blood sugar, bones. No pillar has more than 2 pieces. Skipped: CX11 (financial news only), mood (thin, caution), and the gray-market retatrutide angle (crowded this week). The retatrutide FDA classification Short is held until the court rules, since that ruling could qualify as Lane C.

pieces.topic: What happens when you stop tirzepatide: the SURMOUNT-4 randomized withdrawal trial (adults with obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related condition, without diabetes), why appetite returns (biology, not willpower), how many people stop early in real-world data, and what the evidence suggests about keeping results
pieces.angle: Keep the same structure and title. Chapter 4: cite only persistence studies you can locate and open (for example Gasoyan 2026 DOM doi 10.1111/dom.70660; Ulrich 2026 DOM doi 10.1111/dom.70535, which is GLP-1 receptor agonists in type 2 diabetes with no tirzepatide). Label each one 'observational' and name the drugs and population it covered. Drop the 'DOCC' citation unless the Scriptwriter can find and verify the actual paper. Say that cost and access drove many discontinuations. Present SURMOUNT-4 regain as group averages from weeks 36 to 88, and source the 'biology, not willpower' line to mechanism or label sources, not to SURMOUNT-4. pieces.why: A named playbook Lane A example (Lane A median 26, Strength Training growing) with high search demand. The randomized SURMOUNT-4 evidence holds up under fact-check, and the new real-world persistence papers give it a timely hook. | fact-check: The core topic is fine for Lane A. SURMOUNT-4 (Aronne et al., JAMA 2024) is a real randomized withdrawal trial in adults with obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related condition, without diabetes: a 36-week open-label lead-in, then randomization to continued tirzepatide or placebo for weeks 36 to 88. Take every per-arm % change, n and estimand from the JAMA paper. Chapter 3 is fine if it only uses the secondary outcomes the paper reports. The problem is chapter 4. I could not find an 'Oct 2026 Diabetes Obes Metab' persistence paper or any study called 'DOCC'. The real-world discontinuation papers I could confirm are: (a) Gasoyan et al. 2026, Diabetes Obes Metab, doi 10.1111/dom.70660, the Cleveland Clinic study of weight change after stopping semaglutide or tirzepatide (observational; most people went on to other obesity treatments); (b) Ulrich et al. 2026, Diabetes Obes Metab, doi 10.1111/dom.70535, a UK cohort of GLP-1 receptor agonists in type 2 diabetes. It covers dulaglutide and semaglutide, with no tirzepatide, and found a 41.1% one-year discontinuation risk; (c) the PMC12515774 academic obesity clinic paper, where only 5% of patients were on tirzepatide. Cost and access were major reasons people stopped in the real-world data, so don't frame stopping as a personal failing. Keep 'regain' as an average result, not something that happens to everyone. Keep the appetite biology to mechanism sources, not to SURMOUNT-4, which measured weight and not hunger. The ending CTA must name 'Strength Training on Tirzepatide' by its exact live title, oEmbed-verified.

pieces.topic: Is semaglutide safe if your kidneys are already weaker? Safety outcomes by chronic kidney disease severity in the FLOW trial (Kidney International, Oct 20, 2026)
pieces.angle: Before scripting, find and verify the Kidney International Oct 20, 2026 paper. If it can't be found, build the Short on what is confirmed: FLOW's main result (type 2 diabetes plus CKD, semaglutide 1.0 mg weekly versus placebo, primary kidney outcome 19% versus 23%, HR 0.76, median 3.4 years), the CJASN 2026 finding that kidney and survival benefits were consistent across eGFR and albuminuria levels, and, as a whole-trial result, fewer serious adverse events on semaglutide (49.6% versus 53.8%) but more stopping because of GI side effects at every eGFR level. Keep the title as a question with no 'safe' claim, e.g. 'Semaglutide With Weaker Kidneys: What the FLOW Trial Found'. Keep the eGFR/urine albumin check and dehydration actions, 'don't stop or change your medicines on your own', 'Not personal advice' and the full prescriber line.
pieces.working_title: Semaglutide and Weaker Kidneys: What the FLOW Trial Found #shorts
pieces.why: A fresh FLOW paper with little coverage on a common worry. The body-worry format works on YouTube (about 104) and is our top Instagram format (reach 112). Semaglutide-only is allowed because the evidence covers semaglutide only. | fact-check: FLOW is real: adults with type 2 diabetes and CKD, semaglutide 1.0 mg weekly versus placebo, 3,533 participants, median follow-up 3.4 years. Its main kidney result was HR 0.76 for the primary kidney composite. But I could not confirm a FLOW secondary analysis in Kidney International dated Oct 20, 2026. The CKD-severity analyses I could confirm are: (a) WCN25-1900 'Clinical and Safety Outcomes of Semaglutide by CKD Severity in the FLOW trial', an abstract in Kidney International Reports; (b) Tuttle et al. 2026, 'Kidney and Survival Outcomes with Semaglutide by CKD Severity in the FLOW Trial', CJASN, which covers efficacy, not detailed safety. What those sources report on safety: fewer serious adverse events on semaglutide than placebo overall (49.6% vs 53.8%), and more GI-related discontinuations on semaglutide across the full eGFR range. Don't write 'safe for weaker kidneys'. Write 'in this trial population, the safety results were broadly similar across kidney-function levels' only if the source says so. Give 1.0 mg only as the trial arm, never as advice. Semaglutide only, so no tirzepatide claims and no #Tirzepatide. The 'follow for more' ending is fine.

pieces.topic: Tirzepatide vs semaglutide in type 2 diabetes: the SURPASS-2 randomized head-to-head (NEJM 2021, adults with type 2 diabetes on metformin, 40 weeks)
pieces.angle:
13:00 lead, two-drug head-to-head with tirzepatide named first. It uses a different trial from previous Shorts (SURMOUNT-5 has already been used).

Answer by 10 s: in about 1,879 adults with type 2 diabetes on metformin, A1C fell more on all 3 tirzepatide doses than on semaglutide 1 mg at 40 weeks. Give per-arm A1C (with mmol/mol) and weight change, copied exactly from NEJM, with per-arm n and the estimand.

Key honesty line: the semaglutide dose was 1 mg, lower than the 2.4 mg weight-loss dose, and this was open-label. It's a different population from SURMOUNT-5. GI side effects for each drug, using per-arm figures from the paper.

'Bigger average isn't best for everyone; don't switch, stop or change your medicines on your own.' 'Not personal advice' plus the full prescriber line, then 'follow for more'. 170 words or fewer. Captions keep numbers whole and match the stat pills exactly.

pieces.topic: Why does hunger come back after stopping tirzepatide? The SURMOUNT-4 regain result in one number
pieces.angle:
20:00 funnel Short and spin-off of L1. It asks one fresh question rather than re-cutting the L1 script.

Answer by 10 s: one SURMOUNT-4 figure, the weight change from week 36 to 88 on placebo vs continued tirzepatide, with per-arm n, population (no diabetes) and estimand, matching L1's verified numbers exactly. One line of biology: the medicine was turning down appetite signals, and when it stops those signals return. That's biology, not willpower.

Say 'don't stop or change your medicine on your own; plan any change with your prescriber.' One GI line. 'Not personal advice' plus the full prescriber line.

Last spoken line: 'Full breakdown: [L1's exact live title], on our channel.' Write it only if L1's URL is oEmbed-confirmed at script time. Put that URL on description line 1 and in the pinned comment. Otherwise end with 'follow for more' and don't count it toward Exp D.

170 words or fewer, mixed at masking 0.02 or lower.

pieces.topic: Do GLP-1 medicines affect your bones? The Archives of Osteoporosis systematic review (Oct 23, 2026), reused from the verified, published 10-25 Short
pieces.angle:
Minimum-effort carousel built only from the verified 10-25 bones Short script, with no new research. Drop it if that script isn't confirmed as verified.

Slides:
(1) The worry, named as understandable.
(2) 8 small randomized trials in adults with overweight or obesity, mostly exenatide and liraglutide, one semaglutide trial, no tirzepatide. Use the n exactly as verified.
(3) Very low certainty: too thin to tell whether these drugs help, spare or harm bone, and fracture trials are needed.
(4) Losing weight by any method can come with some bone loss.
(5) Recommended habits, not proven on the drug: muscle-strengthening at least 2 days a week, started gently, and a protein food at each meal unless your clinician has told you to limit protein.
(6) If you have osteoporosis or fracture risk, ask your clinician about bone health. Common GI side effects. 'Don't stop or change your medicines on your own.'
(7) 'Not personal advice' plus the full prescriber line.

No emoji, no scare visuals, no #Tirzepatide.
